title: How Almerico and Sharkey brought jazz back
summary: Riddick explains that Tony Almerico played Sundays at the Parisian Room, then Sharkey's band was a hit and twenty jazz bands sprang up.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Drove you crazy with all that kind of stuff. This is the third reel on it. Los Angeles country. I didn't hear what you were saying. I was setting the machine up. Pam asked you about big name entertainment here. They used to have more of it. There used to be more big name entertainment.

You see, the thing about it was when we and Tony Almerico's band brought the jazz back. Actually, Tony Almerico had it before we were, but he only played on Sunday afternoon at the Parisian Room. With all the guys like Roy, what's your name, on piano, and Shorty Reese on tenor, and Frank Federico, and all of them. Actually, Julian Lane played trombone. They only played on Sundays, but Tony was playing dances all over this country. And Sharky organized this band, and all of a sudden we were just one huge hit. And then everybody got in on the act. Within six months' time there were twenty bands playing all up, because everybody opened a joint and played jazz.
You got something from the item here on page 17, October the 18th, 1950.
